title: Biological needs supported by the WWOX record, for the repurposing module
status: Non-canonical research material. A need is a place where the record observed something and a pharmacological or other intervention could be aimed. It is not a hypothesis, a ranking, a claim of benefit or medical advice. Nothing here changes the four scientific current files.

track.B: variant- or lesion-specific (an allele class, a splice site, a stop codon)

goal.deep_recovery: aims to restore the lost WWOX function itself
goal.partial_benefit: aims at a concrete partial benefit, symptom control or protection of function

vocabularies.track_and_goal_note: The two fields are independent: gene addition is Track A with goal deep_recovery; a splice correction is Track B with goal deep_recovery; an ISR lever is Track A with goal partial_benefit.

evidence_scope.WWOX_EXPERIMENT_IN_DEE_SYSTEM: measured in a WWOX-deficient system that models the disease (the bridge's definition): patient case, patient-derived or engineered knockout cells (including non-neural cells such as fibroblasts and mouse embryonic fibroblasts), organoids, mouse animals. A non-neural system carries no implied transfer to neurons; the observation's limits say so. model_type human_clinical_report marks an uncontrolled case or series.
evidence_scope.WWOX_BIOLOGY_OTHER_CONTEXT: WWOX outside a model of the disease (the bridge's definition): a fly amyloid model or other invertebrate knockdown, a cancer line, a construct expressed in unrelated cells, or a contrast that carries no genotype comparison. Model type is on each observation.
evidence_scope.OTHER_DISEASE_PRECEDENT: a precedent from another disease (never WWOX evidence)
evidence_scope.COMPUTATIONAL_RESULT: an analysis of deposited data or a prediction made inside this repository (transcript, not flux; exploratory)
evidence_scope.UNVERIFIED_HYPOTHESIS: no observation: a premise or a placeholder (the bridge's UNQUALIFIED is the nearest label; the other five values are the bridge's own EVIDENCE_SCOPES)

direction.up: raise the target level or activity
direction.restore: return a lost function or level toward normal
direction.uncertain: a direction is proposed in the record but its sign is unresolved or context-dependent

vocabularies.certainty: free text beginning with one of: supported_in_WWOX_mouse_model, supported_as_clinical_report_only, inferred, context_dependent, unknown (a trailing clause may qualify it)

locator_status.MANIFEST: points at an entry of a deepdive manifest; the checker verifies the entry exists and that the anchor text occurs in it
locator_status.DOCUMENT: points at a repository document by path; the checker verifies the file exists
locator_status.REGISTRY_ONLY: names registry record ids only; the checker verifies the ids resolve
locator_status.GAP: no locator exists; the gap is explicit

target_kind.intervention_target: a protein a drug or modality named in the record would act on (class-level where no compound is named)
target_kind.pathway_member: a pathway member or substrate that explains the mechanism but is not itself the proposed point of action
target_kind.readout_marker: a marker or differentially expressed gene used as a readout; being differentially expressed does not make it a therapeutic target
target_kind.disease_gene_product: the WWOX gene or its product, the lesion itself
target_kind.effector_constraint: a gene whose manipulation the record argues against (e.g. Tau is the effector of the benefit)
target_kind.identity_guard: listed to prevent a symbol or naming confusion, not as a target

basis.observed: at least one observation is a WWOX measurement (in a DEE-relevant system or in another context)
basis.exploratory_question: no WWOX measurement: only a premise, a placeholder or a repository-computed result; read as a question to measure, not as a need with evidence

reading_rules: An observation is what a source measured; INFERRED lists what the record does not measure.
Association is not modulation, and modulation is not rescue. A readout level (transcript, protein, phospho, activity, flux) is stated per observation and never promoted.
intervention_direction never assumes that reversing an observed change is beneficial. certainty and do_not_assume say so.
A need with only UNVERIFIED_HYPOTHESIS or COMPUTATIONAL_RESULT scope is a question, not an established need; scope is carried so a consumer can filter.
Hypothesis ids are references. Status and ranking live in the hypothesis ledger only.

provenance.no_new_reading: No paper was newly read for this table. Each observation is carried from a card, a manifest entry, a registry record or a repository analysis, and says which.

hgnc_snapshot.verification: All HGNC ids and the collision notes were checked against the live HGNC REST service (rest.genenames.org, read-only, no registration) on 2026-10-28; the 91 symbols returned the stored ids.
hgnc_snapshot.earlier_source: The ids were first taken from hgnc_complete_set_20261022.json (untracked shared files tree, sha256 below), which is not in git.

provenance.pathway_ids: Gene Ontology identifiers; each id and label was looked up against the EBI QuickGO term service on 2026-10-28 (key-less, read-only). GO:0030433, first entered, is obsolete and was replaced by GO:0036503. A pathway id is a search hint for the term, not a statement that WWOX acts in that process.

needs.label: Restore WWOX protein in neurons by gene addition (AAV-type vector)

track.basis: Gene addition is lesion-independent: it supplies a working copy whatever the allele (map CHAIN A: 'genotype-agnostic'). Track A is stated on that ground, not on the depth of the aim.

goal.basis: Aims to restore the lost function itself (survival, growth, glycaemia, behaviour, myelin, gliosis and spike-wave discharges were measured as endpoints in the Wwox-null mouse).

observed.statement: Neonatal intracerebroventricular neuron-promoter AAV9-WWOX in the Wwox-null mouse: the high-dose arm reaches a survival plateau of about 76-77 percent to day 300 (wild-type control arm itself ends near 71-72 percent), the low-dose arm falls to 0 percent by about day 77; low dose is nonetheless better than untreated knockout.
observed.genotype: constitutive Wwox deletion (FVB), treated versus untreated knockout and wild type
observed.age_stage: neonatal injection (efficacious window stated as P0 to P5), follow-up to day 300
observed.comparison: high-dose versus low-dose versus untreated knockout versus wild type
observed.direction_observed: improved by treatment: progressive extinction at the low dose, plateau at the high dose
observed.limits: Two doses only, so a threshold and a steep gradient cannot be told apart (the source entry refuses 'a step and not a gradient'); the dose unit convention is not declared by the source; observations at P300 are survivor-selected.

locators.anchor: high dose is not distinguishable from wild type

observed.statement: The same study: high-dose spike-wave discharges per hour fall from about 0.635 (knockout) to about 0.13 (treated), not different from wild type (about 0.03); no low-dose arm exists for this endpoint.
observed.age_stage: about two to three weeks after birth, 7 days of recording
observed.comparison: treated high dose versus untreated knockout versus wild type (n 5 per group)
observed.limits: High dose only; n 5; panel read at 400 dpi.

observed.statement: Neuron-specific (Synapsin-Cre) deletion reproduces the phenotype, myelin deficit included, whereas oligodendrocyte-specific and astrocyte-specific deletions show no evident anomaly; the myelin deficit is about 3.3 times fewer myelinated axons in the corpus callosum at P17 (authors' own counts).
observed.genotype: Synapsin-Cre Wwox deletion versus oligodendrocyte (Olig2-Cre) and astrocyte (GFAP-Cre) deletions
observed.limits: Powered at the axon/field level, three mice per genotype; the oligodendrocyte and astrocyte result is a flat negative that the paper turns into its central inference.

inferred: That gene addition would recover a manifested deficit: in the mouse every endpoint is measured after neonatal treatment (main cohorts P0-P1; timing arms P1-P5 in S8, small n, no P4 survival) of animals never measured before it (prevention or early-window). The only post-onset add-back is organoid hyperexcitability at week 10 to 16 (post-onset by about three weeks, different organoid cohorts, week 16 only, persistence not measured), which did not correct radial-glia abnormalities.

That a lower dose than the high-dose arm would still help, or that it would not: with two doses the shape of the dose-response is not determined, and no expression difference was measured between the two doses in seven of eight regional comparisons (entry 12).
Partial restoration may suffice in genotype classes that retain a missense allele (inference from a human genotype-phenotype series; not tested).

intervention_direction.rationale: Neuron-restricted loss reproduces the phenotype and neuron-restricted restoration rescued several endpoints in the Wwox-null mouse.
intervention_direction.do_not_assume: No ceiling is measured. Ectopic WWOX moved some readouts beyond wild type in organoids, and applied recombinant WWOX lowered viability of human ESC-derived cortical neurons in disease and isogenic control lines (preprint). More is not safer.

counter_evidence: Rescue is not normalisation: unmyelinated axons per field remain about 52 versus about 26 in wild type; the paper's text states that treated knockout mice exceeded wild type in motor coordination and learning (Figure 4K), and the record's count of exceeding panels (three of eight) is not adjudicated (map CHAIN A, CLAIM 004, CLAIM 011).

The neuron-promoter vector corrected neuronal function without correcting radial-glia abnormalities (organoid arm), and layer-marker SATB2 mRNA overshoots wild type up to about eleven-fold in treated organoids.

Two doses cannot distinguish a threshold from a steep gradient (manifest entry 40); the low dose shows progressive extinction (0 percent at about day 77), the high dose a plateau; no intermediate dose was run.
The post-natal window is untested in the source; progenitor/radial-glia defects are largely prenatal (CLAIM 014).

sources.hypotheses_note: HYP-20261025-09 is referenced only for its gene-therapy signal (Wnt effectors overshoot under rescue); there is no hypothesis whose subject is gene addition.

coverage.note: Coverage of this need by catalogue compounds is not computed here; the repurposing module sets it.

needs.notes: Gene addition is a modality, not a repurposing-catalogue compound class; kept as a need so that restoration-level comparators exist for every downstream need. The goal reads 'deep recovery' as an aim; the evidence is early-window prevention plus one organoid post-onset functional recovery. Do not carry a perinatal result to a later intervention.

needs.label: Restore correct WWOX transcript from a canonical splice-acceptor allele (splice-switching, editing)

track.basis: Allele-class specific: the lesion is a canonical splice-acceptor variant; the strategy only applies to that class.

goal.basis: Would restore the transcript and so the protein.

observed.statement: Human blood cDNA across exon 6: the c.517-2A>G homozygote yields only the shorter product (504 bp, interpreted as an 89 bp exon-6 deletion); patients of another genotype class in the same source show two products (593 and 504 bp). Products were sequenced per the Methods.
observed.genotype: c.517-2A>G, homozygous patients; other genotype classes in the same source
observed.comparison: patient genotype classes against each other
observed.limits: Blood, not brain; the Results frame the shorter product as consistent with prediction, not as a displayed junction read; a different acceptor allele from the c.1057-2A>G worked example. Non-neural (non-brain) cells: no transfer to neurons is implied.

observed.statement: For the c.1057-2A>G reference-class worked example the record holds predictions only: SpliceAI acceptor loss (DS_AL) 0.96, a cryptic acceptor gain (DS_AG) 0.64 at +8, and MaxEntScan 7.28 to -0.67; no transcript measurement of this allele exists in the sources read.
observed.limits: Predictions, not measurements. The record's own note shows the +8 cryptic acceptor gives opposite frame outcomes under two coordinate conventions: under SpliceAI's standard convention it is an in-frame 6 nt deletion (a hypomorph, not a null); under the other it is a frameshift. The note favours the first reading with 'suggestive, not decisive' strength.

inferred: That the reference acceptor allele is null-like at transcript level (no wild-type transcript) is a prediction-based inference.
Which exon-skipped product is made, whether it escapes nonsense-mediated decay, and whether it is translated, is unmeasured for the reference allele.

Whether the allele is null-like: under the standard SpliceAI coordinate convention the +8 cryptic acceptor would give an in-frame 6 nt deletion (a hypomorph); the frameshift reading depends on the other convention (splice-allele RNA note). Which product is made, and whether it escapes nonsense-mediated decay, is unmeasured for this allele.

intervention_direction.on: aberrant-to-normal transcript ratio for the acceptor allele
intervention_direction.rationale: If the allele loses its wild-type transcript, restoring normal splicing would restore the product; whether this allele is null-like or a hypomorph depends on the unresolved cryptic-site outcome, so the sign of the need is conditional.
intervention_direction.certainty: inferred (conditional on the unresolved cryptic-site outcome)
intervention_direction.do_not_assume: Splice-switching oligonucleotides mask elements and do not create splice sites; expert guidance classifies variants within 5 bp of the boundary or with destroyed canonical splicing as not eligible (map N-10). Base or prime editing is the open arm and is gene editing, not repurposing.

counter_evidence: N-10: the 5 bp positional rule and the 'destroyed canonical splicing' class are expert-consensus criteria, not an experiment; the map itself notes that faint wild-type bands can still make a case suitable and that membership of the 'destroyed' class is unmeasured for this allele.
Exon 9 is the last exon and carries the stop codon and the last residues of the SDR domain; in-frame skipping is not available.
The exon-6-skipped product of the measured c.517-2A>G allele was detectable and sequenced in blood, so the transcript is not eliminated there; nonsense-mediated decay was not tested.

sources.hypotheses_note: HYP-20260709-06 is the exon-9 inclusion assay (biomarker and ASO endpoint); referenced by id only.

targets.role: pre-mRNA / transcript target (exon 6 and exon 9 as named in the map)

coverage.note: Coverage of this need by catalogue compounds is not computed here; the repurposing module sets it.

needs.notes: Oligonucleotide and editing modalities are outside a small-molecule repurposing catalogue; the need is kept so that a transcript-level comparator exists.

needs.label: Read-through of a premature stop codon in a WWOX nonsense allele

track.basis: Allele-class specific: only applies to alleles with a premature stop codon.

goal.basis: Would restore full-length protein from the affected allele.

observed.statement: No read-through experiment on WWOX was found in the sources read, and a systematic enumeration of nonsense alleles now exists only as a PREDICTION from sequence (IT4 E1a, 2026-10-28, independently re-derived: 32 single-nucleotide stop-gained alleles of NM_016373.4 in the repository ClinVar snapshot, undated; 23 predicted NMD-sensitive, 1 borderline p.Trp335*, 8 predicted to escape, all in exon 9; the NMD classes are predictions by the 50-55 nt rule, never measurements). Nonsense alleles ARE recorded in this repository's therapeutic-class census, from published reports: p.(Arg54*), p.(Trp44*), p.(Arg264*), p.(Gln191*) and p.Trp218*, each with patients listed, none with an NMD assay, and flagged there as read-through candidates (a repository remark, not a measurement); all five are predicted NMD-sensitive. The reference genotype class (destabilising SDR missense plus canonical splice-acceptor allele) carries no premature stop in the stated analysis, so read-through has no applicable target there: an inference from classification, not evidence that read-through fails, and it stays open for nonsense alleles of other lesion classes. Caveat carried from the E1a note and its independent verification: the unmeasured intron-8 retention outcome predicted for the exon-9 acceptor splice allele would create a stop codon, so even the inference 'no applicable target in the reference genotype class' rests on an unmeasured prediction about that allele.
observed.limits: The census rows are curation of published cohorts, many of which pool splice, nonsense, frameshift and CNV into one 'null' bin; the 'candidate' flag is not evidence. The zero for read-through agents is bounded (WWOX-literature sweep and a title/abstract PubMed query, not re-runnable offline).

inferred: Whether any WWOX-DEE allele is read-through-amenable is not established: no read-through or NMD measurement on a recorded nonsense allele exists in the sources read. Whether a recorded nonsense allele escapes NMD is predicted by position (23 sensitive, 1 borderline, 8 escape of 32 ClinVar alleles) and not measured.

intervention_direction.on: full-length WWOX protein from a premature-stop allele
intervention_direction.rationale: Conditional on a nonsense allele that is translated without escaping nonsense-mediated decay; nonsense alleles are recorded but no measurement shows that.
intervention_direction.do_not_assume: A candidate (amlexanox) was qualified and not promoted; no repurposing claim follows.

counter_evidence: No WWOX read-through datum exists in either direction.

sources.hypotheses_note: No hypothesis in the ledger has read-through as its subject.

coverage.note: Coverage of this need by catalogue compounds is not computed here; the repurposing module sets it.

needs.notes: Nonsense alleles are recorded, but there is no WWOX measurement that read-through would address (no NMD assay, no protein readout); the need is an exploratory question about whether the recorded alleles are amenable.

needs.label: Rescue a destabilised SDR-domain missense WWOX protein (folding, quality control, degradation)

track.basis: Lesion-specific: concerns an SDR missense allele class (p.Gln230Pro is the worked example); a null or splice allele has no protein to rescue.

goal.basis: Aims to return functional WWOX from the mutant allele.

observed.statement: Patient-derived fibroblast line homozygous for p.Gln230Pro: WWOX transcript is comparable to reference lines, but no WWOX band is detected on one western membrane at one exposure (confirmed on a second harvest of the same line).
observed.comparison: patient line against three non-fibroblast reference lines (two cancer lines, HEK293); no control fibroblast
observed.limits: One donor line, one membrane, one exposure, no healthy fibroblast lane; the transcript comparison is against non-fibroblast lines with one bar per line, no n and no error bars; non-neural cells; lysate fraction not separated; the cause (synthesis, solubility or turnover) is unresolved. Non-neural (non-brain) cells: no transfer to neurons is implied.

locators.anchor: no band in three knockout clones and in the patient fibroblast lane

observed.statement: A different SDR missense (P252A), stably over-expressed in non-neural thyroid-carcinoma cell lines (CAL-62, BCPAP): the P252A protein is much lower than wild type while its mRNA is not decreased; a cycloheximide chase shows faster turnover; chloroquine and ammonium chloride restore the protein, MG-132 and 3-MA do not (this repository's census); the abstract names HSC70-mediated chaperone-mediated autophagy, which the manifest reads as the authors' speculation, and abundance and function are confounded. The other missense tested (P282A) shows no stability defect; both mutants lose tumour-suppressive activity and P282A loses POLE4 binding. A cancer proband homozygous for both did not have WWOX-related nervous-system disease (35 years old at admission, per the Results).
observed.tissue_or_cells: thyroid-carcinoma lines CAL-62 and BCPAP (non-neural); one proband's germline genotype
observed.limits: Constructs over-expressed in unrelated cell lines (not a model of the disease); MG-132 did not accumulate even wild-type WWOX, so the proteasome negative is weakly informative; the P252A band is faint and the lines are not expression-matched; the cohort is one proband.

locators.anchor: p4_card.novelty_for_woree: repository reading of the HSC70 co-immunoprecipitation and the lysosome/proteasome sensitivity (the manifest entries cited do not carry those two details)

inferred: That the Q230P lesion is a degradation problem rather than a synthesis or solubility problem is not known; every proteostasis route below inherits that.
That raising abundance raises function: severity tracks residual function, not abundance (CLAIM 030), and 'stable but inert' is a demonstrated phenotype for some variants.

That a fold gain in mutant protein is useful: a boost multiplies the residual function R (amount relative to wild type times function per molecule) and does not change it, so parity needs the reciprocal of R; R is unmeasured for every WWOX allele, and for the Q230P class the only bound is the unquantified detection floor (IT5 P8, missense_recovery_it5_p8_20261029).

Whether a stabilised Q230P-class protein would be active depends on the lesion class, which is unmeasured: in one cytosolic enzyme (CBS) the same route blocker restored function to the transgenic wild-type range in some animals for a regulatory-domain allele, improved it for three catalytic-domain alleles, not at all for one, and a stable but catalytically impaired allele was not rescued; whether a Q230P-class protein resembles either class is open (domain label and modelled burial only); the outcome for one allele also differed between a mouse liver and a kidney cell line (IT6 P6, broad_recovery_it6_p6_20261029; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE).

intervention_direction.on: functional (not merely detectable) mutant WWOX protein
intervention_direction.rationale: The protein is not detected while the transcript is reported comparable; restoring the product from this allele would require raising functional protein, if the lesion is a protein-level bottleneck (unresolved).
intervention_direction.do_not_assume: Direction is conditional on the unresolved bottleneck. Chemical chaperones were judged to act in the wrong compartment (map N-11), an objection that IT5 P8 narrowed: it is not established for a soluble cytosolic client (Munc18-1, where the class and two HDAC-free osmolytes raised a mutant and a class-I HDAC inhibitor did not; no enzyme and no WWOX system tested; an HDAC6 role is open); HSP70 co-induction carries a hypothesis of harm (N-12); proteasome inhibition is a probe-derived rescue idea that also stabilises misfolded protein. ER/UPR modulators have no stated target because WWOX is a cytosolic enzyme and no measurement places the variant in ER quality control.

counter_evidence: Q230P is not P47T and not P252A; no read-across between missense alleles (MECHANISM_TRANSFER_FIREWALL).
Abundance restored without function would be neutral at best (CLAIM 030).

N-11: 4-phenylbutyrate/TUDCA act on an ER-chaperone rationale and WWOX is cytosolic. N-12: HSP70 co-induction could stabilise an insoluble protein (adjacent-protein precedent: stabilisation gave insoluble protein without activity).

IT5 P8: in the one soluble cytosolic precedent the treatment gains on mutant protein were small (about 1.05 to 1.65 fold total on four of five variants) against a deficit of tens of fold, and the same gain applies to wild type; a measured turnover difference of about 1.5 to 3 fold explains only part of that deficit, so the cleared-after-synthesis branch is not the only candidate (NOT WWOX EVIDENCE; reader arithmetic on panel estimates).

IT6 P6: in a cytosolic enzyme (CBS) proteasome inhibition raised wild-type half-life about 7.7-fold, so the gain is a boost for wild type too; tolerated exposure lowered homocysteine by about half without a significant activity gain and with immune-cell toxicity, gave no significant change for S466L, and effective exposure was toxic; protein rose with activity unchanged for one allele under HSP70 or HSF1 co-expression; ASPA C152W stabilised protein was exclusively insoluble with no activity detectable. For the only WWOX missense with a measured turnover (P252A) the route was lysosomal and a proteasome inhibitor did not even accumulate wild type, in stable-overexpression thyroid-cancer lines; MG-132 also left the normal-size protein unchanged in 49 cancer lines (PMID 14695174) (NOT WWOX EVIDENCE for the CBS and ASPA items).

needs.label: Raise endogenous WWOX expression (CRISPRa, anti-miR, small-molecule activators)

track.basis: Which lesion is treated decides whether this can work. With a null or splice-null allele there is little template to raise. With a missense allele whose protein is not made despite normal transcript (Q230P in the one measured line) the bottleneck is downstream of transcription and a boost could amplify a non-functional product. Only an allele that yields residual functional protein is a plausible substrate. The effect is allele-dependent, so Track B; it is not variant-independent.

goal.basis: Aims to raise functional WWOX.

observed.statement: Neuronal CRISPRa Wwox upregulation in the Drosophila amyloid model improved lifespan (median 47.5 versus 29 days) and climbing, and had no significant effect without amyloid.
observed.genotype: neuronal CRISPRa Wwox upregulation (not RNAi) with neuronal Abeta42 versus Abeta42 alone
observed.age_stage: adult; climbing at days 14 and 21, lifespan to death
observed.comparison: upregulation against control with and without Abeta42
observed.limits: A fly amyloid model, not WWOX-DEE; wild-type Wwox allele; the model type label is the nearest available, the manipulation is CRISPRa; benefit occurred without a reduction in Ldh or 2-hydroxyglutarate.

observed.statement: In the one measured p.Gln230Pro system (a fibroblast line) the protein is not detected although the transcript is reported comparable (one bar per line, no n); a bottleneck after transcription is inferred, not measured.
observed.limits: One donor line; see NEED-WWOX-MISSENSE-PROTEIN-RESCUE. Non-neural (non-brain) cells: no transfer to neurons is implied.

inferred: That a non-allele-specific boost would amplify the missense allele and push more aberrant transcript toward nonsense-mediated decay on the splice allele is inferred (map N-05).

intervention_direction.on: WWOX transcript/protein from a functional allele
intervention_direction.rationale: Only where a functional or partly functional allele exists.
intervention_direction.do_not_assume: Neither too little nor too much WWOX: WWOX is pro-apoptotic in some contexts, and no ceiling measurement was found in the sources read.

counter_evidence: N-05: the target is not the bottleneck for Q230P; a boost is an allele-asymmetric amplifier.
Fly benefit does not transfer to DEE or to a mammalian allele.

sources.hypotheses_note: HYP-20260709-02 (boost alone has an uncertain sign) and -03 (anti-miR-153) are referenced by id.

needs.label: Integrated stress response (eIF2alpha-ATF4) activity: attenuate a possible over-activation

track.basis: Downstream and allele-blind; Track B (Q230P class) is unmeasured.

goal.basis: A downstream lever cannot restore WWOX function; deep recovery stays with WWOX restoration.

observed.statement: Neuronal Wwox knockdown raises Atf4 immunofluorescence (about 1.0 to about 1.28, six brains per group) in the presence of neuronal Abeta42 (Mann-Whitney U 0, P 0.0022, six brains per group); in the no-amyloid background the same comparison was not significant (t 0.0894, P 0.9305, six brains; 95% interval about plus or minus 1.3 pooled SD), and no interaction test between the two backgrounds is reported.
observed.genotype: neuronal Wwox RNAi plus neuronal Abeta42 versus control RNAi plus Abeta42; LacZ background for the no-amyloid contrast
observed.tissue_or_cells: adult fly brain, four small regions of interest
observed.comparison: knockdown against control, with and without Abeta42
observed.direction_observed: up in the amyloid background; not significant in the no-amyloid background (separate tests, no interaction test)
observed.limits: Not WWOX-DEE evidence; n 6; y axis not at zero; Atf4 is never perturbed in the paper; PERK, GCN2 and eIF2alpha phosphorylation are not measured; the no-amyloid arm is a non-significant test, not a demonstrated absence, and the dependence on amyloid is a difference in significance between two separate tests (re-read 2026-10-28, isr_kinase_interactome_atf4_reconciliation_it4_20261028.md section 4); the Xbp1 reporter (IRE1 arm) is non-significant at about 15 brains and cannot be read as evidence for PERK.

observed.statement: Human WWOX-knockout cerebral organoid transcriptome: the canonical ATF4/ISR target set is LOWER than 10,000 random sets (P 0.0005; exploratory, six libraries, uncorrected across nine set tests); 12 canonical targets, mean shift -0.288; CHAC1, TRIB3 and PHGDH are individually down, while ATF4, ATF5, DDIT3, ASNS and others are not individually significant and ATF4 transcript is flat; the UPR-branch set does not differ from chance. SESN2 (-0.35) is also individually down. The disclosure in the source: CHAC1, TRIB3 and PHGDH had been seen before the gene sets were fixed, so their per-gene direction is not a blind result (the set-level test was not looked at beforehand).
observed.genotype: WWOX knockout (4 libraries) versus wild type (2 libraries)
observed.comparison: knockout against wild type, set-level against random sets
observed.limits: Transcript, not eIF2alpha phosphorylation or ATF4 protein; no amyloid; the shift is as consistent with a less advanced tissue as with a WWOX effect.

observed.statement: Adults with ALS: the eIF2B activator DNL343 showed target engagement in a phase 1b abstract, and a 24-week placebo-controlled trial showed no benefit (ratio 1.04, credible interval 0.83 to 1.32).
observed.limits: Abstract-level, other disease, adults; says nothing about a developmental encephalopathy.

observed.statement: Children with vanishing white matter (an eIF2B lesion): a single-arm phase 1/2 abstract reports hazard ratio 0.33 (0.16 to 0.69) against matched registry controls, with serious adverse events in about three quarters of 33 children, hallucinations in over half and severe constipation in three. The card does not state that the agent is an eIF2B activator.
observed.direction_observed: benefit with a large adverse-event burden (non-randomised)
observed.limits: Abstract-level, non-randomised, a disease whose lesion is the ISR regulator; a tolerability dataset here is not suitability for WWOX-DEE.

observed.statement: 5xFAD amyloid mouse: an eIF2B activator improved recognition memory and lowered microglial activation and tau, without reducing amyloid burden; phospho-eIF2alpha was lower.
observed.age_stage: adult; Results state 5-7 days and Methods 4-6 days (the source is inconsistent); larval development

observed.statement: The d-APV arm of the burst experiment is 5 slices from 3 animals (51 bursts; the paper's tests are on bursts) at postnatal day 13 to 17, d-APV 50 uM; the d-APV bar carries no significance marker in Fig 3D (bursts absent, no variance). observed.limits: Fig 3D read by eye from a JPEG; the two printed baselines differ about 2.7-fold and the paper does not explain it (a rate from the median interval against a median of per-slice rates is a possibility, unverified); any graded block read from bursts needs long recordings per condition (F04).

inferred: That bursting reflects a gain of NMDAR or AMPAR function rather than a permissive dependence (the sign of a partial block is untested).

That the same node is shared with GRIN-variant epilepsies (convergence argument); in a retrospective GRIN-variant series, memantine benefit split by variant class (14 of 19 gain-of-function versus 3 of 15 loss-of-function/indeterminate), so a shared node does not give the sign. The authors call 4 of the 15 comparator variants non-pathogenic.

That the depolarised resting potential (O6), together with the halved inhibitory current amplitude (O3), relieves the voltage-dependent magnesium block of NMDAR enough to explain the NMDAR dependence of the burst: arithmetic in the IT6-P11 record (other cell type, simple occupancy model), never tested in a WWOX system.

That the d-APV dependence is NMDAR gain: three readings fit it (gain of NMDAR current; permissive necessity in a network whose pyramidal neurons are depolarised (O6) and receive about half the inhibitory current (O3); AMPAR-led drive), they are not exclusive, and the data separate none of them and rank none (F04).

intervention_direction.rationale: A perturbation result, not a reversal inference: blocking NMDAR with d-APV abolished the burst in the WWOX-deficient slice (one drug, one preparation).
intervention_direction.certainty: supported_in_WWOX_mouse_model for the tool compound; unknown for any clinically used antagonist
intervention_direction.do_not_assume: Full competitive block is not a partial block. Memantine and perampanel were not found to have been given to a WWOX system in the sources read. Chronic NMDAR block may cost activity-dependent myelination (unmeasured). Raising extracellular Mg2+ is the physiological way to lower NMDAR gain, but no Mg2+ manipulation has been done in a WWOX system, the incubation ACSF already contains magnesium and the recording bath is not stated (O7), and the one mouse study read found that an oral magnesium sulfate left cerebrospinal-fluid magnesium unchanged: do not equate a supplement with a bath concentration, and do not treat the open-label infant trials of magnesium sulfate with ACTH as evidence about this node. A pore blocker's potency depends on voltage, extracellular Mg2+ and intracellular Ca2+, so a memantine result at the Mg2+ level of the incubation solution (1.3 mM; the recording bath is not stated) is not a GluN2A/2B block unless the Mg2+ level is reported; an effect of a subunit-selective tool (a GluN2B NAM) is an effect of that tool, not of a different drug (F04).

counter_evidence: Only a full competitive block (d-APV) has been tried; whether the dependence is permissive or a gain is untested.
Memantine accelerated provoked seizures in an adult rat model; paediatric effectiveness of memantine is not established on its label (card F01).
One adult WWOX case on perampanel plus six drugs had no sustained benefit (n 1).
Pannexin-1 blocker arm went the wrong way untested (map N-16); gap-junction node withdrawn pending occlusion.

In the one randomised open-label infant trial read with an oral phase (West syndrome, 48 analysed; three days of intramuscular magnesium sulfate then oral, ACTH and antiseizure drugs in both arms) magnesium did not change seizure control (p 0.69); the positive randomised signal used intravenous magnesium sulfate with ACTH and is abstract-level.
The magnesium arithmetic gives a modest reduction for a modest rise in extracellular Mg2+, against the complete block of d-APV.

A competitive full-block NMDAR antagonist (selfotel) failed in adult stroke and head-injury trials (stroke: early mortality imbalance; head injury: stopped for concern about deaths and futility, later analysis without a significant mortality difference); NMDAR blockade in the developing rat brain triggers apoptotic neurodegeneration (abstract level); memantine failed two controlled paediatric studies in another disorder and has no paediatric effectiveness on its label (F04).
The d-APV arm carries no significance marker in Fig 3D, the tests are on bursts not animals, and the baseline burst frequency is printed twice with different values (O8).

inferred: That oxidative stress contributes to WWOX-DEE pathology in neurons: not measured in a DEE system in the sources read.

intervention_direction.do_not_assume: Antioxidants (NAC, CoQ10, creatine) rest on an assumed monotonic loss-to-ROS relation that the record refutes as an assumption.

counter_evidence: N-14: relationship is not monotonic; sign is context-dependent.

extension_path.summary: A new study enters as an observation; it either amends an existing need or opens a new one. Editing a need is an ordinary revision of the file.
steps: 1. The study has a manifest in disease-models/wwox/research/deepdive_manifests/ with verbatim locators (a full-text read with a receipt). A study without a manifest may enter only as a document or registry locator, and its locator_status says so.

2. Write the observation with the six-part context (system, genotype, tissue, age/stage, comparison, readout), its readout_level, the direction observed, the evidence_scope and the limits the source itself states.

3. Decide: does it fit an existing need's target or pathway? If yes, append it to that need's observed list, and re-read that need's inferred, intervention_direction and counter_evidence: a new observation can move any of them. If no, open a new need with the full field set.
4. Keep track and goal as two fields. Keep hypothesis ids as references; never copy a hypothesis ranking into this table.
5. Add HGNC symbols and ids and say when a symbol collides with another gene or a former symbol. Add pathway ids only after looking them up.
6. Run: python3 disease-models/wwox/research/drug_repurposing/needs/check_needs.py   (offline) and the test in the same directory.
